Modern.brandNameRationale: Parse is the word every developer knows. It's the verb for understanding what code or input means. Short, technical, immediately legible to the audience. One syllable. Hard P, soft S.
Modern.industrySummary: Developer tools have entered a second wave. The early big tools (GitHub, Stripe, Vercel) set the design bar. New entrants have to clear it. Modern brand work is now table stakes for serious devtools.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Vercel (vercel.com) set the modern monochrome template. Linear (linear.app) made dev brand feel like good design software. Stripe (stripe.com) is the gold standard for documentation as brand. We are designing for the rung below those names.
Modern.positioningStatement: Developer tools that explain themselves the first time.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most devtools fail at the docs. Our brand promise is that you can read the homepage and the API reference in fifteen minutes and start shipping. The brand sounds the way the product reads.

targetAudience.primary: Software engineers, 25 to 45. Three to fifteen years of experience. Reads Hacker News at lunch. Pays attention to brand even if they say they don't. Will switch tools the second the docs annoy them.

dos: Write like a senior engineer documenting for the next one
Show code in the first paragraph
Be specific about what the tool does and does not do

Modern.logoDirection: A clean wordmark in a custom geometric mono. PARSE in all caps, tight kerning, with a small caret symbol used as a separator in compound use (PARSE > Docs). The caret can stand alone as a favicon and app icon.

colorPalette.name: Editor Black
colorPalette.meaning: The dark theme background. The native habitat of the customer.

colorPalette.name: Syntax Blue
colorPalette.meaning: The color of a keyword in a familiar editor.

typography.secondary: JetBrains Mono for code samples and the wordmark
typography.rationale: Inter is the dev-default for marketing pages. A real coding font for code samples and the wordmark. No serif anywhere.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No marketing fluff. No founder-on-stage moments on the homepage. No glassmorphism. No hero illustration of abstract figures pushing data through tubes.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Westgate sounds like a firm that has been around. It could be a London office building, a Boston law partnership, a Swiss watch atelier. Systems anchors it as B2B software. Not what you would expect from a developer tools brand. That is the point.
Luxury.story: Westgate began with a question. What would a developer tools company look like if it took itself as seriously as the customer takes their work? The answer was a slower roadmap, a tighter team, and a brand that doesn't shout.
Luxury.industrySummary: Most premium B2B software signals premium by being expensive. There's a smaller market for premium that signals premium by being restrained. Long-running, slow-roadmap, deeply documented tools. Companies that don't churn out features for the announcement.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: JetBrains (jetbrains.com) is the closest peer in restraint and seriousness. Charm (charm.sh) has the right confidence at smaller scale. We position above the marketing-driven brands and beside the craft-driven ones.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Developer tools for teams that buy slowly and stay long.

targetAudience.primary: Senior engineering leaders at companies of 200 to 5000 engineers. They sign three-year contracts. They expect a vendor to be around in five.

dos: Speak to the leader, not the user

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark with deliberate spacing. A small geometric mark, two perpendicular lines forming a quiet right angle, used as a hallmark on documents, hardware, and the IDE plugin marketplace.

colorPalette.name: Oak
colorPalette.meaning: The color of an old desk in a serious room.
colorPalette.usage: Wordmark, primary brand color, foiled documents

typography.primary: Tiempos Text for the wordmark and major type
typography.secondary: Söhne for product UI and docs
typography.rationale: A classical serif for the brand surface. A modern grotesk for the product surface. Each does its job and gets out of the way.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No quarterly feature announcements. No conference circuit. No social media presence for the company. No founder personal brand on Twitter.

Luxury.brandDescription: Developer tools for teams that buy slowly and stay long.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: stdin is the Unix term for standard input. Lowercase always. The audience reads the brand name the same way they read the rest of their terminal. No translation needed. No marketing.
Minimal.industrySummary: Developer tool websites have all started to look the same. Big gradient. Loud heading. Animated illustration. There's room for one that looks like a man page.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Suckless (suckless.org) is the philosophical ancestor. cat-v (cat-v.org) is the visual cousin. Most modern devtools are too design-driven to occupy this space.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Developer tools that look like the terminal you use them in.

targetAudience.primary: Engineers who live in the terminal. They use neovim or emacs by choice. They read documentation as plain text. They distrust most marketing pages by default.

dos: Show the command, then explain it

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. stdin in monospace, lowercase, set without decoration. No icon. No second mark. The favicon is the four letters stacked.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No hero illustrations. No glass cards. No gradient text. No animations on scroll. No SaaS-stock photography. No sans-serif anywhere.

Minimal.brandDescription: Developer tools that look like the terminal you use them in.
Minimal.mission: To build developer tools that look like the terminal you use them in.
Minimal.vision: There's room for one that looks like a man page.
coreValues: Plain — plain language survives every translation.
Technical — the spec is the position.
Honest — including when the answer is one we'd rather not give.
Precise — accuracy is the brand.
Minimal.scope:
stdin delivers by:
• Write in plain text
• Show the command, then explain it
• Use mono font everywhere

Corporate.tagline: Enterprise developer platform, built for scale.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: A keystone holds the arch up. The whole structure depends on it. Systems is the procurement-friendly closer. The pair reads as something Fortune 500 already bought and forgot they bought, in a good way. Trustworthy. Permanent.
Corporate.industrySummary: Enterprise development platforms are a category worth billions, dominated by a handful of legacy players. New entrants have to thread the needle between modern usability and procurement-friendly seriousness.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: GitHub Enterprise (github.com/enterprise) is the standard. GitLab (gitlab.com) the open-source-leaning competitor. JetBrains Space (jetbrains.com/space) the developer-first one. CircleCI (circleci.com) and Jenkins (jenkins.io) own the CI/CD side. We compete on a unified platform story.
Corporate.positioningStatement: One platform for code, builds, security, and compliance, built for companies that take all four seriously.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Procurement at large companies wants fewer vendors. We win when we can replace four point solutions with one platform and pass the compliance audit on the first try.

targetAudience.primary: VPs of Engineering, CTOs, and CISOs at companies with 1000 to 50000 employees. They sign multi-year contracts and they live with the consequences.

dos: Speak to the buyer, not the developer
donts: Promise more than the platform delivers

Creative.brandNameRationale: Every developer has a favorite hotkey. The brand is named after the small daily move that feels good and saves time. The name is short, all-caps, and reads like a stamp on a sticker.
Creative.manifesto: Most developer tools take themselves seriously, which is fine, but it's also boring. We made Hotkey because building software should be fun more often than it is. The product is serious. The brand is not.
Creative.industrySummary: Developer brand has gotten quite uniform. Monochrome. Mono font. Quiet illustration. There's room for one that's loud, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and still ships a great product.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Linear (linear.app) is the design standard. Vercel (vercel.com) the monochrome standard. Charm (charm.sh) the closest to our personality. Cal.com (cal.com) does playful well. We are louder than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: Developer tools with personality, made by people who think work should be fun.

targetAudience.primary: Engineers 22 to 40. Working at small to mid-size companies. Posts on Twitter and Bluesky. Buys stickers for the laptop. Picks tools based on vibes as much as features.

dos: Make jokes that land for engineers
Use real screenshots, not stock illustrations
Talk to one developer at a time
donts: Use the words synergy, paradigm, or transform

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display sans, with the second K stylized as a small keyboard key (the rounded square outline). Standalone keyboard-key icon for app icons, stickers, and avatar use.

colorPalette.name: Hot Pink
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero buttons, social

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and UI
typography.rationale: Migra carries the personality. Neue Montreal handles UI without losing character. The pair feels designed but human.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not enterprise. Not monochrome. Not afraid of stickers. Not too cool to be helpful.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Laptop stickers. Conference T-shirts that engineers actually want. A monthly changelog written like a friend's update. A community Discord that has rules and personality. Real screenshots in every blog post.
